subject.title: feat(hooks): emit session:aborted + opt-in auto-continue hook

question: Should OpenClaw expose `session:aborted` as a supported internal hook event and ship the disabled-by-default `auto-continue` recovery behavior in core once the recovery dispatch is made non-blocking?
rationale: This is a new session lifecycle event and bundled autonomous behavior, not a repair of an established public contract; implementation correctness cannot determine whether that product surface should be maintained.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in recovery hook
options.body: Keep the event and bundled hook, first make dispatch non-blocking and require current-head gateway proof of resume and budget behavior.

options.title: Expose only the event
options.body: Retain a generic non-blocking abort event for integrations but leave automatic continuation to external hooks or plugins.

options.title: Decline the new surface
options.body: Keep the existing watchdog abort behavior and close this feature direction rather than adding an automatic recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in recovery hook
recommendation.body: Keep the event and bundled hook, first make dispatch non-blocking and require current-head gateway proof of resume and budget behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and review context connect this person to the current hook enable-policy model and the trust-boundary design relevant to this decision.
